Data

ACS-5
```{r}
years <- c(2024)

state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]  

my_vars <- c(
  # Population & demographics
  tot_pop       = "B01003_001",
  median_age    = "B01002_001",
  white         = "C02003_003",
  black         = "C02003_004",
  asian         = "C02003_006",
  hispanic      = "B03001_003",

  # Economic wellbeing
  medhhinc      = "B25119_001",
  pop_poverty   = "B17001_002",
  pop_poverty_universe = "B17001_001",
  labor_force   = "B23025_003",
  unemployed    = "B23025_005",

  # Housing
  hu_ownocc     = "B25003_002",
  tot_hu        = "B25001_001",
  rent_burden_30_35   = "B25070_007",  # 30.0-34.9%
  rent_burden_35_40   = "B25070_008",  # 35.0-39.9%
  rent_burden_40_50   = "B25070_009",  # 40.0-49.9%
  rent_burden_50plus  = "B25070_010",  # 50.0%+
  rent_total          = "B25070_001",
  avg_hh_size   = "B25010_001",

  # Education
  edu_hs_or_less     = "B15003_017",
  edu_bachelors_plus = "B15003_022",
  edu_total          = "B15003_001",

  # Family structure
  divorced_m    = "B12001_010",
  divorced_f    = "B12001_019",
  single_dad_children = "B11003_010",   # male householder, no wife, with own children <18
  single_mom_children = "B11003_016" ,
# female householder, no husband, with own children <18
married_m     = "B12001_004",
  married_f     = "B12001_013"
)


census_data_tract <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {
  map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
    get_acs(
      geography = "tract",
      variables = my_vars,
      year = yr,
      state = st,
      survey = "acs5",
      geometry = FALSE,
      cache_table = TRUE
    ) %>%
      mutate(year = yr)
  })
}) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  arrange(NAME, year)

census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(divorced = divorced_m + divorced_f,
         married  = married_m + married_f)

census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(
    divorce_rate = divorced / tot_pop * 100,
    marriage_rate = married /tot_pop * 100
  )
```


Prisons (ICPSR)
```{r}
#US Prisons (from ICPSR)
#The raw dataset contains 6,468 prison facilities with geographic boundaries.
#Two filters are applied: (1) only facilities with STATUS "OPEN" or "CLOSED" are
#retained, dropping ambiguous or unknown statuses; (2) TYPE "COUNTY" is excluded,
#removing local jails which were not sited as economic development tools and do not
#fit the theoretical framework of the study. The cleaned dataset is then collapsed
#to the county level using COUNTYFIPS, producing counts and capacity/population
#totals broken out by status (open, closed, and combined).

prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson")




nrow(prisons_icpsr)
st_crs(prisons_icpsr)
sum(!st_is_valid(prisons_icpsr))   # check for broken geometries before doing anything else



prisons_icpsr <- st_make_valid(prisons_icpsr)

sum(!st_is_valid(prisons_icpsr))   # should now be 0

prisons_centroids <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  st_centroid()

nrow(prisons_centroids)   # should still be 6468 - no facilities lost



state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]

tract_geo <- map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
  tracts(state = st, cb = TRUE, year = 2020)
}) %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

nrow(tract_geo)
st_crs(tract_geo)
sum(!st_is_valid(tract_geo))



tract_geo <- st_transform(tract_geo, st_crs(prisons_centroids))

st_crs(tract_geo) == st_crs(prisons_centroids)   # MUST print TRUE


prisons_with_tract <- st_join(prisons_centroids, tract_geo, join = st_intersects)

nrow(prisons_with_tract)              # should equal 6468 exactly
sum(is.na(prisons_with_tract$GEOID))  # facilities whose centroid fell outside every tract



prisons_facility_clean <- prisons_with_tract %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(
    STATUS %in% c("OPEN", "CLOSED"),
    TYPE != "COUNTY",
    !is.na(GEOID)   # drop the 52 unmatched facilities, as discussed
  )

nrow(prisons_facility_clean)

prisons_by_tract <- prisons_facility_clean %>%
  group_by(GEOID) %>%
  summarise(
    num_prisons     = n(),
    num_open        = sum(STATUS == "OPEN"),
    num_closed      = sum(STATUS == "CLOSED"),
    capacity_total  = sum(CAPACITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_open   = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_closed = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_total       = sum(POPULATION, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_open        = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_closed      = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

nrow(prisons_by_tract)


```

Death counts
```{r}
#death counts and death rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm injuries by census tract of residence


injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/injury_overdose_violence_census_tract.csv")

injury_overdose_violence_exploded <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  separate_rows(NAME, sep = ",\\s*") %>%          # split combined tract lists into one row per real tract
  rename(real_tract_geoid = NAME) %>%
  mutate(real_tract_geoid = str_trim(real_tract_geoid))

# Sanity check: these should now be clean 11-digit real Census tract GEOIDs
head(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid, 10)
nchar(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid[1])

#2022
injury_overdose_violence_2022 <- injury_overdose_violence_exploded %>%
  filter(Period == "2022") %>%
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide", "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(real_tract_geoid, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME, Period),
    names_from  = Intent,
    values_from = Rate,
    names_glue  = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate,
    GEOID = real_tract_geoid,
    year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    suicide_rate  = ifelse(suicide_rate  == -999, NA, suicide_rate),
    homicide_rate = ifelse(homicide_rate == -999, NA, homicide_rate),
    overdose_rate = ifelse(overdose_rate == -999, NA, overdose_rate)
  )

nrow(injury_overdose_violence_2022)
n_distinct(injury_overdose_violence_2022$GEOID)
```

Urban vs. Rural counties (USDA)
```{r}
# Load and reshape the USDA rurality file
rural_2023 <- read_csv("data/rural_urban_codes2023.csv")  # 1-3: urban, 4-9: rural

rural_2023 <- rural_2023 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Attribute, values_from = Value) %>%
  mutate(
    Population_2020 = as.numeric(Population_2020),
    RUCC_2023 = as.numeric(RUCC_2023)
  )

rural_2023_clean <- rural_2023 %>%
  rename(county_geoid = FIPS) %>%
  mutate(rural = as.integer(RUCC_2023 >= 4))

# Drop any previously-joined rurality columns (including any .x/.y duplicates
# left over from earlier attempts), so this can be re-run safely from a messy state
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  select(-matches("^RUCC_2023(\\.[xy])?$"),
         -matches("^rural(\\.[xy])?$"),
         -matches("^Population_2020(\\.[xy])?$"))

# Derive each tract's county FIPS from its own GEOID (first 5 characters)
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(county_geoid = str_sub(GEOID, 1, 5))

# Join county-level rurality onto every tract within that county
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  left_join(rural_2023_clean %>% select(county_geoid, RUCC_2023, rural, Population_2020),
            by = "county_geoid")

# Sanity checks
names(census_data_tract)
sum(is.na(census_data_tract$RUCC_2023))
nrow(census_data_tract)



#2013
# The 2013 Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) from the USDA are already in wide
# format with one row per county. The only cleaning needed is renaming FIPS to GEOID
# for consistency with the join key used across all other datasets, and creating a
# binary rural indicator following the standard USDA convention where codes 1-3
# denote metro (urban) counties and codes 4-9 denote nonmetro (rural) counties.
# The 2013 vintage is used rather than 2023 because it predates the 2019 outcome
# year, which is the methodologically appropriate choice.

#rural_2013 <- read_excel("data/rural_urban_codes2013.xls")

#  rename(GEOID = FIPS) %>%
#  mutate(rural = as.integer(RUCC_2013 >= 4)) %>%
#  select(GEOID, State, County_Name, Population_2010, RUCC_2013, rural, Description)
```

Cleaning the dataset

```{r}
# Rate/percentage variables - transfers cleanly from the county-level version
facility_level_dataset <- facility_level_dataset %>%
  mutate(
    poverty_rate       = pop_poverty / pop_poverty_universe * 100,
    unemp_rate         = unemployed / labor_force * 100,
    pct_white          = white / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_black          = black / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_asian          = asian / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_hispanic       = hispanic / tot_pop * 100,
    homeown_rate       = hu_ownocc / tot_hu * 100,
    pct_bachelors_plus = edu_bachelors_plus / edu_total * 100,
    pct_hs_or_less     = edu_hs_or_less / edu_total * 100,
    rent_burdened_30plus_rate = (rent_burden_30_35 + rent_burden_35_40 + rent_burden_40_50 + rent_burden_50plus) / rent_total * 100,
    single_parent_rate = (single_dad_children + single_mom_children) / tot_hu * 100
  )

# Preserve both facility name and tract name - these are NOT duplicates here
facility_level_dataset <- facility_level_dataset %>%
  rename(facility_name = NAME.x, tract_name = NAME.y)

# Save
write_csv(facility_level_dataset, "data/final/facility_level_dataset.csv")
```


## Analysis

```{r}
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

# Go back to the pre-exploded data and count how many real tracts were
# bundled into each original CDC-reported row
tract_group_size <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  filter(Period == "2022", Intent == "Drug_OD") %>%
  mutate(n_tracts_in_group = str_count(NAME, ",") + 1) %>%
  select(NAME, n_tracts_in_group) %>%
  separate_rows(NAME, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  rename(GEOID = NAME) %>%
  mutate(
    GEOID = str_trim(GEOID),
    group_type = if_else(n_tracts_in_group == 1, "Standalone (own rate)", "Combined (shared rate)")
  ) %>%
  distinct(GEOID, group_type, n_tracts_in_group)

# Join this classification onto your NY tract outcome data
ny_tract_grouped <- ny_tract_outcome %>%
  left_join(tract_group_size, by = "GEOID")

table(ny_tract_grouped$group_type, useNA = "ifany")
```







```{r}
# Reproject to a projected (meters-based) CRS before computing distances -
# WGS84/NAD83 are angular (lat/lon degrees), so distances computed directly
# in that CRS are distorted; a projected CRS like Albers Equal Area (EPSG:5070,
# standard for CONUS) gives real, interpretable distances in meters
tract_geo_proj <- st_transform(tract_geo, 5070)
prisons_centroids_proj <- st_transform(prisons_centroids, 5070)

tract_centroids <- st_centroid(tract_geo_proj)

# Distance matrix: every tract x every prison facility
dist_matrix <- st_distance(tract_centroids, prisons_centroids_proj)

# For each tract, find the minimum distance (nearest facility) in meters, convert to miles
tract_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi <- apply(dist_matrix, 1, min) / 1609.34

# Attach back to your tract-level data
tract_dist <- tract_centroids %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, dist_to_nearest_prison_mi)

summary(tract_dist$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi)
```

```{r}
#install.packages("nngeo")
library(nngeo)
nearest <- st_nn(tract_centroids, prisons_centroids_proj, k = 1, returnDist = TRUE)
tract_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi <- unlist(nearest$dist) / 1609.34

summary(tract_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi)
head(tract_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi, 10)
```

```{r}
tract_dist <- tract_centroids %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, dist_to_nearest_prison_mi)

nrow(tract_dist)

# Merge into your tract-level outcome data
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  left_join(tract_dist, by = "GEOID")

sum(is.na(census_data_tract$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi))
```
